name: Stargardt Disease

criteria.description: Progressive bilateral central vision loss beginning in childhood or adolescence
Presence of characteristic yellowish-white pisciform flecks at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium in the macula and mid-periphery
Electroretinogram (ERG) showing normal or mildly reduced rod and cone responses
Identification of pathogenic variants in the ABCA4 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive bilateral central vision loss with characteristic fundus findings and/or pathogenic ABCA4 gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is increasingly used to confirm diagnosis; ERG may help differentiate from other retinal dystrophies.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents in childhood or adolescence
searchTerms: gradual loss of central vision both eyes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of pisciform (fish-tail shaped) yellowish-white flecks in the macula

pathognomonic.notes: Macular atrophy develops as disease progresses
searchTerms: worn down spots in eye center

common.notes: Light sensitivity common in affected individuals

common.symptomName: Difficulty adapting to low light (nyctalopia mild or absent)
common.notes: Night vision usually preserved but may be mildly affected

occasional.notes: Night vision difficulties in some cases

imaging: Fundus autofluorescence showing characteristic flecks and areas of atrophy
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealing loss of photoreceptor layer and retinal pigment epithelium atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ABCA4 gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Electroretinogram (ERG) typically normal or mildly reduced cone and rod responses

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of vitelliform lesions rather than pisciform flecks
Later onset compared to Stargardt disease
More widespread photoreceptor dysfunction affecting cones and rods
ERG shows markedly reduced cone and rod responses
More rapid progression of vision loss
Presence of drusen rather than pisciform flecks
Different genetic and environmental risk factors

redFlags: Presence of significant peripheral vision loss
Signs of optic neuropathy or neurological deficits
references: Allikmets R, et al. A photoreceptor cell-specific ATP-binding transporter gene (ABCR) is mutated in recessive Stargardt macular dystrophy. Nat Genet. 1997.
Stone EM. Genetic testing for inherited eye disease. Arch Ophthalmol. 2007.
Fujinami K, et al. Clinical and molecular analysis of Stargardt disease. Ophthalmology. 2013.
